claim: All proteins diffused freely in HeLa cell cytoplasm with Dconfocal values of 18–30 µm²s⁻¹.
source: The proteins showed Dconfocal values of 18–30 µm2s–1 in HeLa cell cytoplasm, which is typical for a cytoplasmic protein diffusion coefficient (Figure 2E).
evidence: The manuscript reports measured diffusion coefficients from FRAP experiments for 16 proteins in HeLa cells.

claim: Full FRAP recovery was observed for all proteins, indicating free diffusion.
source: Moreover, full FRAP recovery was observed, indicating free diffusion.
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental FRAP recovery measurements for proteins.

claim: The 16 proteins studied have predicted pKa values of 4.5–8.
source: Appendix 1—table 1 provides the predicted isoelectric points and net charges at pH 7.4 of the purified proteins as calculated by Prot Pi, showing pKa values of 4.5–8, which are representative of the majority of E. coli cytosolic proteins.
evidence: The manuscript references calculated pKa values from computational prediction software.

claim: Acidic and neutral proteins do not stick to the HeLa cell cytoplasm or membranes, even if not in their native environment.
source: The results show that acidic and neutral proteins, even if not in their native environment, do not stick to the HeLa cell cytoplasm or membranes.
evidence: This is inferred from the free diffusion and full FRAP recovery observed for E. coli proteins expressed in HeLa cells.

claim: Fluorescein has a Dconfocal of 56.5±2.4 µm²s⁻¹ in PBS.
source: We found that the diffusion coefficient of fluorescein in PBS (Dconfocal of 56.5±2.4 µm2s–1) was reduced to Dconfocal of 38.5±2.0 µm2s–1 in HeLa cytoplasm (Figure 3C).
evidence: The manuscript reports measured diffusion coefficients from FRAP experiments.

claim: Fluorescein has a Dconfocal of 38.5±2.0 µm²s⁻¹ in HeLa cytoplasm.
source: We found that the diffusion coefficient of fluorescein in PBS (Dconfocal of 56.5±2.4 µm2s–1) was reduced to Dconfocal of 38.5±2.0 µm2s–1 in HeLa cytoplasm (Figure 3C).
evidence: The manuscript reports measured diffusion coefficients from FRAP experiments.

claim: Fluorescein has a Dconfocal of 43.2±2.2 µm²s⁻¹ in the cell nucleus.
source: In the cell nucleus, a value of Dconfocal of 43.2±2.2 µm2s–1 was determined, while in concentrated HeLa cell extract (equivalent protein concentration of ~100 mg/mL), Dconfocal of 49.6±1.9 µm2s–1 was measured.
evidence: The manuscript reports measured diffusion coefficients from FRAP experiments.

claim: Fluorescein has a Dconfocal of 49.6±1.9 µm²s⁻¹ in concentrated HeLa cell extract (~100 mg/mL protein concentration).
source: In the cell nucleus, a value of Dconfocal of 43.2±2.2 µm2s–1 was determined, while in concentrated HeLa cell extract (equivalent protein concentration of ~100 mg/mL), Dconfocal of 49.6±1.9 µm2s–1 was measured.
evidence: The manuscript reports measured diffusion coefficients from FRAP experiments.

claim: The faster Dconfocal of fluorescein in cell extract compared to live-cell cytoplasm may result from the higher crowding density of the latter.
source: The faster Dconfocal in cell extract compared to live-cell cytoplasm may result from the higher crowding density of the latter.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed difference in diffusion rates.

claim: The lowering of diffusion coefficients of negatively charged fluorescein correlates with the increasing crowding density of the medium moving from simple buffer to cells.
source: The lowering of diffusion coefficients of negatively charged fluorescein correlates with the increasing crowding density of the medium moving from simple buffer to cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the trend observed in the measured diffusion coefficients across different media.

claim: After 24 hr incubation with fluorescein, the fractional recovery dropped from 0.95 to 0.65.
source: While micrographs did not show dye aggregation inside the cell cytoplasm (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B) and diffusion rates are similar to those determined by microinjection (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D), the fractional recovery dropped from 0.95 to 0.65.
evidence: The manuscript reports measured fractional recovery values from FRAP experiments comparing microinjection to 24 hr incubation.

claim: A fraction of fluorescein is immobile in the cell after 24 hr incubation.
source: This suggests that a fraction of fluorescein is immobile in the cell after 24 hr incubation, and is not diffusing.
evidence: This is inferred from the reduced fractional recovery after 24 hr incubation.

claim: CCF2 has a pKa of ~5.1.
source: CCF2 is a fluorogenic substrate used for monitoring β-lactamase activity, with a pKa of ~5.1 (Zlokarnik et al., 1998).
evidence: The pKa value is cited from a published reference.

claim: CCF2 diffusion rates are about half as fast as those measured for fluorescein.
source: Its calculated Dconfocal values in PBS and inside cells are about half as fast as those measured for fluorescein (Figure 3E–G), and its fractional recovery is ~0.7.
evidence: The manuscript reports measured diffusion coefficients from FRAP experiments comparing CCF2 to fluorescein.

claim: CCF2 has a fractional recovery of ~0.7.
source: Its calculated Dconfocal values in PBS and inside cells are about half as fast as those measured for fluorescein (Figure 3E–G), and its fractional recovery is ~0.7.
evidence: The manuscript reports measured fractional recovery from FRAP experiments.

claim: No sign of CCF2 aggregation is seen in micrographs inside the cell cytoplasm or nucleus.
source: No sign of aggregation is seen in micrographs inside the cell cytoplasm or nucleus (Figure 3G).
evidence: The manuscript reports observations from microscopy images.

claim: The substantial slower rate of recovery and lower fractional recovery of CCF2 relative to Fluorescein suggests its diffusion to be obstructed within the cell.
source: The substantial slower rate of recovery, and lower fractional recovery of CCF2 relative to Fluorescein suggests its diffusion to be obstructed within the cell.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed differences in FRAP measurements between CCF2 and fluorescein.

claim: The observed substrate limited enzymatic degradation of CCF2 in HeLa cells is a consequence of its occlusion within the cellular cytoplasm.
source: This is in line with our prediction, that the observed substrate limited enzymatic degradation of CCF2 in HeLa cells is a consequence of its occlusion within the cellular cytoplasm (Zotter et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a prediction supported by the current FRAP data and cited from previous work.

claim: CF514 has a pKa value of ~3.
source: The sharp changes of the UV- spectrum at pH~3 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A, B), as well as the redshift confirms a pKa value of ~3.
evidence: The pKa value was determined from pH-dependent UV-spectrophotometry measurements.

claim: CF514 has a Dconfocal of ~61.1 ± 3.0 µm²s⁻¹ in PBS.
source: Dconfocal in PBS was ~61.1 ± 3.0 µm2s–1, and 26.3±1.9 and 29.2±2.0 µm2s–1 in the cell cytoplasm and nucleus of HeLa cells, respectively (Figure 3I).
evidence: The manuscript reports measured diffusion coefficients from FRAP experiments.

claim: CF514 has a Dconfocal of 26.3±1.9 µm²s⁻¹ in HeLa cell cytoplasm.
source: Dconfocal in PBS was ~61.1 ± 3.0 µm2s–1, and 26.3±1.9 and 29.2±2.0 µm2s–1 in the cell cytoplasm and nucleus of HeLa cells, respectively (Figure 3I).
evidence: The manuscript reports measured diffusion coefficients from FRAP experiments.

claim: CF514 has a Dconfocal of 29.2±2.0 µm²s⁻¹ in the nucleus of HeLa cells.
source: Dconfocal in PBS was ~61.1 ± 3.0 µm2s–1, and 26.3±1.9 and 29.2±2.0 µm2s–1 in the cell cytoplasm and nucleus of HeLa cells, respectively (Figure 3I).
evidence: The manuscript reports measured diffusion coefficients from FRAP experiments.

claim: CF514 has ~90% recovery after FRAP.
source: The FRAP curves look similar to fluorescein (Figure 3H–J), with ~90% recovery after FRAP.
evidence: The manuscript reports measured fractional recovery from FRAP experiments.

claim: The drop of CF514 Dconfocal in cells is attributed to cellular crowding.
source: The drop of Dconfocal is attributed to cellular crowding.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed reduction in diffusion rate in cells compared to buffer.

claim: Acidic small molecules diffuse well inside cells.
source: The results so far show that acidic small molecules diffuse well inside cells.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the FRAP measurements of fluorescein, CCF2, and CF514.

claim: GSK3 inhibitor SB216763 has a pKa of 7.0.
source: The GSK3 inhibitor SB216763 (pKa = 7.0, M.W.=371 Da, Figure 1) aggregates when dissolved in PBS buffer solution.
evidence: The pKa value is stated as a property of the compound.

claim: GSK3 inhibitor SB216763 aggregates when dissolved in PBS buffer solution.
source: The GSK3 inhibitor SB216763 (pKa = 7.0, M.W.=371 Da, Figure 1) aggregates when dissolved in PBS buffer solution.

claim: Aggregation of GSK3 inhibitor SB216763 can be reversed by adding BSA.
source: However, in our previous study we have seen that aggregation of this particular small molecule drug can be reversed by adding BSA and the extent of de-aggregation depends on the amount of BSA added (Dey et al., 2022).

claim: The extent of de-aggregation of GSK3 inhibitor SB216763 depends on the amount of BSA added.
source: However, in our previous study we have seen that aggregation of this particular small molecule drug can be reversed by adding BSA and the extent of de-aggregation depends on the amount of BSA added (Dey et al., 2022).
evidence: This is cited from a previous study by the authors.

claim: SB216763 has a Dconfocal of ~0.61 ± 0.03 µm²s⁻¹ in HeLa cell cytoplasm.

claim: SB216763 has a fraction recovery of 0.8 after 10 s in HeLa cell cytoplasm.

claim: SB216763 diffusion in HeLa cell cytoplasm is ~40-fold slower compared to measurements in 50 mg/mL BSA protein solution.
source: This is an ~40-fold reduction in Dconfocal compared to measurements in 50 mg/mL BSA protein solution, where SB216763 is not aggregating (Dconfocal~21.4 ± 0.5 µm2s–1 and fractional recovery of ~0.9 - Figure 4A–C).

claim: SB216763 has a Dconfocal of ~21.4 ± 0.5 µm²s⁻¹ in 50 mg/mL BSA protein solution.
source: This is an ~40-fold reduction in Dconfocal compared to measurements in 50 mg/mL BSA protein solution, where SB216763 is not aggregating (Dconfocal~21.4 ± 0.5 µm2s–1 and fractional recovery of ~0.9 - Figure 4A–C).
evidence: The manuscript reports measured diffusion coefficients from FRAP experiments.

claim: SB216763 has a fractional recovery of ~0.9 in 50 mg/mL BSA protein solution.
source: This is an ~40-fold reduction in Dconfocal compared to measurements in 50 mg/mL BSA protein solution, where SB216763 is not aggregating (Dconfocal~21.4 ± 0.5 µm2s–1 and fractional recovery of ~0.9 - Figure 4A–C).
evidence: The manuscript reports measured fractional recovery from FRAP experiments.

claim: SB216763 is not aggregating in 50 mg/mL BSA protein solution.
source: This is an ~40-fold reduction in Dconfocal compared to measurements in 50 mg/mL BSA protein solution, where SB216763 is not aggregating (Dconfocal~21.4 ± 0.5 µm2s–1 and fractional recovery of ~0.9 - Figure 4A–C).

claim: In cell culture DMEM media (containing 5% serum protein), SB216763 fractional recovery after FRAP is very low.
source: In cell culture DMEM media (containing 5% serum protein) fractional recovery after FRAP is very low (Figure 4A), indicating that the drug is still aggregating (Dey et al., 2022).

claim: Low fractional recovery of SB216763 in DMEM media indicates that the drug is still aggregating.

claim: SB216763 has a Dconfocal of ~11.3 ± 0.7 µm²s⁻¹ in HeLa cell extract.

claim: SB216763 has a fractional recovery of 0.9 in HeLa cell extract.
source: Interestingly, the Dconfocal value in HeLa cell extract was higher ~11.3 ± 0.7 µm2s–1 as is its fractional recovery (0.9), showing that HeLa cell extract, like BSA is disaggregating SB216763.

claim: HeLa cell extract, like BSA, is disaggregating SB216763.
source: Interestingly, the Dconfocal value in HeLa cell extract was higher ~11.3 ± 0.7 µm2s–1 as is its fractional recovery (0.9), showing that HeLa cell extract, like BSA is disaggregating SB216763.

claim: SB216763 colocalizes and is sequestered in acidic chambers of the cell lysosomes.
source: Co-localization with Lysotracker-633 (Figure 4D–E) shows that SB216763 colocalizes and is sequestered in acidic chambers of the cell lysosomes.

claim: SB216763 accumulation into the lysosome increased over time (45-min and 2 hr treatment).

claim: Varying SB216763 drug dosages resulted in Dconfocal values of 0.42–0.61 µm²s⁻¹.

claim: The slow diffusion of SB216763 is not related to its concentration.

claim: Quinacrine DHC has a Dconfocal rate of 41.9±3.0 µm²s⁻¹ in PBS.
source: Quinacrine DHC (M.W.=472.9 Da, Figure 1) is a compound highly soluble in PBS (Dey et al., 2022) with a fast Dconfocal rate of 41.9±3.0 µm2s–1 (Figure 5A–C).

source: This rate dropped to Dconfocal~2.5 ± 0.1 µm2s–1 in HeLa cell cytoplasm, with fraction recovery of ~0.8, in comparison to one in buffer.

claim: Quinacrine DHC has a Dconfocal rate of 15.1±0.6 µm²s⁻¹ in HeLa cell extract.

claim: Quinacrine has a Dconfocal of 2.2±0.1 µm²s⁻¹ following 2 hr incubations.

source: Dconfocal of 4.2±0.2 µm2s–1 was calculated from line-FRAP immediately after micro-injection, slowing to 2.2±0.1 µm2s–1 following 2 hr incubations, with fractional recoveries of 0.63 and 0.57, respectively.

claim: Following 24 hr of incubation, most of the Quinacrine is in the lysosomes.

claim: The low pKa of weakly basic small molecule drugs drive their accumulation in the lysosome.
source: The low pKa of weakly basic small molecule drugs drive their accumulation in the lysosome.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ion trapping of weakly basic drugs.

claim: Weakly basic drugs become protonated in the lysosome, which hinders their back-diffusion to the cytosol.
source: There, they become protonated (ionic form is less-permeable), which hinders their back-diffusion to the cytosol.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ion trapping mechanism.

claim: The phenomenon of drug accumulation in lysosomes is known as cationic ion trapping.
source: The phenomenon is known as cationic ion trapping (Asokan and Cho, 2002; Kaufmann and Krise, 2007) and results in drug accumulation in lysosomes up to millimolar concentrations (de Duve et al., 1974).

claim: Cationic ion trapping results in drug accumulation in lysosomes up to millimolar concentrations.
source: The phenomenon is known as cationic ion trapping (Asokan and Cho, 2002; Kaufmann and Krise, 2007) and results in drug accumulation in lysosomes up to millimolar concentrations (de Duve et al., 1974).

claim: Bafilomycin A1 inhibits the supply of protons to the lysosomal chamber.

source: However, Dconfocal values were not altered much by Bafilomycin A1, as shown in Figure 7—figure supplements 1C and D and 2C and D for GSK3 inhibitor and Quinacrine, respectively.

claim: Dconfocal for GSK3 inhibitor is ~0.60 ± 0.02 µm²s⁻¹ after Bafilomycin A1 treatment.

claim: Dconfocal for Quinacrine is ~2.4 ± 0.1 µm²s⁻¹ after Bafilomycin A1 treatment.
